mainTopic: Who should fast, part-day private fasts and the fast-day prayer, and the questions brought to מר עוקבא
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge. רבי אלעזר praised the one who fasts as holy, but he also said to treat the body as if something holy lives inside it. The גמרא answers that fasting is good only for someone who can handle it. ריש לקיש calls the one who fasts a חסיד. רב ששת and ריש לקיש warn that a תלמיד חכם should not fast, because it weakens his learning. רב ירמיה בר אבא adds that in בבל only תשעה באב is a full public fast. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה. רב הונא rules on when a private faster says the fast-day prayer, and אביי explains that hours never accepted in advance do not count. The amud ends with מר עוקבא, who brings three questions to the בית מדרש: whether one can fast for part of a day, whether gentile wine jars may be used, and what משה wore during the מילואים. A new teaching of רב חסדא begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A person should treat his body as if something holy lives inside it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a teaching that a person should see something holy inside himself. This seems to argue against fasting, which clashes with the earlier praise of the one who fasts as קדוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should think of himself as if a holy one dwells inside his body, as the פסוק says: 'The holy one is in your midst, and I will not come into the city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a teaching of רבי אלעזר: treat your body as if a holy thing lives inside it. It uses this to challenge the earlier idea that fasting makes a person holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If your body holds something holy, you should not weaken it by fasting. Yet the earlier teaching praised the person who fasts and called him קדוש. Both cannot be true without some explanation, so the גמרא must settle the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy; a holy thing or holy one
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: as though a holy one dwells inside his innards,
as it is stated: 'The holy one is in your midst, and I will not come into the city'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's own earlier teaching that one who fasts is called קדוש. His two statements seem to contradict each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A holy thing dwells in the body and should not be harmed, so fasting looks like damage rather than holiness.

steps.title: It depends on whether the person can handle the fast
steps.stepSummary: The two teachings fit different people. One who can fast without harm is praised, and one who cannot should not hurt his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. One teaching is about a person who is able to afflict himself. The other is about a person who is not able to afflict himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by splitting the cases: a person who can bear the fast versus a person who cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise of fasting as holy applies to someone strong enough to fast without damage. The warning to protect the holy body applies to someone who cannot handle it but fasts anyway. Fasting is not good or bad by itself; it depends on the person's ability.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
To afflict himself (to cause himself distress, such as by fasting)

steps.whatToRemember: Fasting is praiseworthy only for someone who can handle it. For someone who cannot, it harms the holy body and should be avoided.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where he is able to afflict himself,
phrases.notes: This is the teaching that praises the one who fasts as holy.

phrases.english: that one is where he is not able to afflict himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — דְּמָצֵי לְצַעוֹרֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by personal ability)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two teachings seem to argue about whether fasting is good at all
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree. Fasting is holy for one who can bear it and harmful for one who cannot.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: one who fasts is called pious
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש praises the person who fasts as a חסיד and brings a פסוק from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: He is called pious, as it says: 'A man of kindness does good to his soul, and one who troubles his flesh...'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש adds his own view: a person who fasts earns the title חסיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads the word גומל as 'holding back' rather than 'doing good.' Read that way, the פסוק praises a person who holds himself back from food. This adds another voice that views fasting positively.

keyTerms.meaning: A pious person, one who goes beyond the basic requirement
Does good to; can also mean weans or holds back

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
he is called pious,
phrases.notes: He means the person who fasts.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'A man of kindness does good to his soul,'
phrases.notes: משלי 11:17. ריש לקיש reads גומל as 'weans,' meaning he holds his soul back from food.

phrases.english: 'and one who troubles his flesh,' etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion about how to view someone who fasts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who fasts is called a חסיד, based on reading גומל as holding back.

steps.title: רב ששת: a תורה student who fasts wastes his meal
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says a yeshiva student who fasts loses out, as if a dog ate his food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: A yeshiva student who sits in a fast, let a dog eat his meal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a sharp warning against fasting for a student who learns תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fasting weakens the student, so he learns less. He gains nothing from his self-denial, as if his portion went to a dog. This sets a limit on the praise of fasting for people whose job is learning.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of the study hall

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
This student of the study hall
who sits in a fast,
let a dog eat his meal.
phrases.notes: The fast weakens his learning, so nobody benefits from the food he skipped. It might as well have gone to a dog.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הַאי בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּיָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the praise of fasting when the faster is a Torah student
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah student should not fast, since it costs him his learning.

steps.title: In בבל, only תשעה באב is a full public fast
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא teaches that בבל has no full public fast except תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: There is no public fast in בבל except for תשעה באב alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה בר אבא gives a rule about which fasts count as a full תענית ציבור in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other community fasts in בבל do not get the full strict rules of a public fast. They are treated more like private fasts. Only תשעה באב has full public-fast status there.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean people in בבל never fasted together. It means their other fasts lacked the full strict rules of a true תענית ציבור.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
There is no public fast in Babylonia
except the Ninth of Av alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא: אֵין תַּעֲנִית צִיבּוּר בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching about fasts, from the same speaker as the next step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only תשעה באב has full public-fast status in בבל.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם may not fast
steps.stepSummary: Quoting ריש לקיש, רב ירמיה בר אבא rules that a תלמיד חכם may not fast, because fasting cuts into his service of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of ריש לקיש: A תלמיד חכם is not allowed to sit in a fast, because he reduces his work for Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a firm rule that a תלמיד חכם is not permitted to fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes further than רב ששת's warning, because it says the scholar is not permitted to fast at all. The reason is that a weaker scholar does less מלאכת שמים, meaning learning and מצוות. It also matches step 2: the praise of fasting does not apply when fasting holds a person back.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of Heaven: Torah study and מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: Fasting may be praiseworthy for others, but a תלמיד חכם should not fast, because it takes away from his learning and service of Heaven.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רַשַּׁאי לֵישֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית,
phrases.english: A Torah scholar is not permitted to sit in a fast,
because he reduces the work of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אֵין תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רַשַּׁאי לֵישֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רב ששת's point into a firm rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may not fast, since it lessens his service of Heaven.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical limit on private fasting. Personal self-denial does not come at the cost of תורה learning.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: eating at night before a fast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that during the first fasts people may eat and drink after dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They eat and drink from after dark,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next line. This is a setup for the ruling that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that during the first set of fasts, eating is allowed the night before. The fast only starts in the morning. That raises a question about a private fast: if you ate all night, does the next day still count as a real fast?

phrases.english: They eat and drink from after dark, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion to the words of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the first fasts, eating is allowed at night and the fast begins in the morning.

steps.title: When a private faster says the fast-day תפילה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a person who accepted a fast says the fast-day prayer even if he ate all night. If he simply kept fasting overnight from the day before, he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירא said in the name of רב הונא: A person who accepted a fast on himself, even if he ate and drank all night, prays the fast-day prayer the next day. If he 'slept in his fast,' he does not pray the fast-day prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the משנה, רב הונא explains when a private faster adds the fast-day prayer, עננו. Eating the night before does not cancel the fast, but extra hours carried over from a fast that already ended do not create a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case he accepted a fast for the coming day, so eating during the night before does not cancel it. In the second case his fast day already ended and he simply kept fasting through the night, and רב הונא says those extra hours do not earn the fast-day prayer. רב הונא does not give a reason. רב יוסף asks for it in the next step, and אביי answers in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Slept over; stayed through the night

steps.whatToRemember: For a private fast, eating the night before does not cancel the fast. But fasting on into the night after the fast ends does not earn the fast-day prayer the next morning.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the one who fasted longer gets 'more' of a fast. He fasted more hours but still does not say עננו. The next two steps work out why.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Huna said:
An individual who accepted a fast upon himself,
even if he ate and drank the whole night,
the next day he prays the prayer of a fast.
phrases.notes: This means adding עננו, 'Answer us on the day of our fast.'

phrases.english: If he slept over in his fast,
phrases.notes: He finished his fast day and kept fasting right through the night.

phrases.english: he does not pray the prayer of a fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: יָחִיד שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's idea of eating at night to a private fast and its prayer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A private fast is set by accepting it for that day. Night eating does not cancel it, and extra fasting carried over does not create a new fast for the prayer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for anyone taking on a private fast: it decides when to add עננו in the עמידה.

steps.title: What is the reason behind רב הונא's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks why רב הונא said that someone who kept fasting overnight does not say תפלת תענית, and offers two possible reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is רב הונא's view? Does he hold that a fast for only part of a day is not a real fast? Or does he hold that it is a fast, but someone fasting for part of a day does not say the fast-day prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks what reason stands behind רב הונא's ruling from step 8. He suggests two possible reasons, and this sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: a fast that is not a full day does not count at all, so the extra night hours are not a fast. Option two: a part-day fast does count, but it does not earn תפלת תענית. Both options would explain why the overnight faster does not say the prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: Fasting for some hours, meaning a fast that is not a full day

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What does Rav Huna hold?
Does he hold: one does not fast for hours,
phrases.notes: "For hours" means a fast that does not last a full day, so it does not count as a fast.

phrases.english: or perhaps: one does fast for hours,
but one who fasts for hours
does not pray the fast-day prayer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב הונא's ruling in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which principle explains רב הונא's ruling: that part-day fasts do not count, or that they count but get no תפלת תענית?

steps.title: אביי: the night hours were never accepted
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב הונא holds that a part-day fast counts and does get תפלת תענית. The overnight hours are different because the person never accepted them ahead of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, רב הונא holds that one can fast for part of a day, and someone who does so says the fast-day prayer. Here it is different, because there are night hours that he did not take on himself from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף with a third reason, different from both of his suggestions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי accepts that part-day fasts are real fasts and earn תפלת תענית. The overnight faster is still left out for a different reason. A personal fast must be accepted beforehand, and those night hours were never accepted, so they are not part of any fast he took on.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (rejects the options just raised)
Accepted upon himself (accepting a fast in advance)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a part-day fast counts and gets תפלת תענית, but only for hours you accepted in advance.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Actually, Rav Huna holds
one does fast for hours,
and one who fasts for hours prays the fast-day prayer.
But here it is different,
for there are hours of the night
that he did not take upon himself from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question with a third explanation
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Part-day fasts count and get תפלת תענית. The night hours were simply never accepted, so they are not part of the fast.

steps.title: מר עוקבא is asked three questions in גינזק
steps.stepSummary: In גינזק, מר עוקבא is asked about part-day fasts, gentile jars, and what משה wore during the מילואים. He has no answer to any of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא came to גינזק. They asked him: Can one fast for part of a day or not? He had no answer. Are gentiles' jars forbidden or permitted? He had no answer. What did משה wear when he served during all seven days of the מילואים? He had no answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which three questions are put to מר עוקבא and he cannot answer any of them. This sets up the answers from the בית מדרש in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question ties into the topic we were just learning: whether a part-day fast counts. The other two questions come along because they were part of the same story. The repeated line "he had no answer" builds toward the בית מדרש's rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not have it (no answer or tradition in hand)
The seven days when the משכן and the כהנים were inaugurated

phrases.english: Mar Ukva happened to come to Ginzak,
they asked him:
Does one fast for hours
or does one not fast for hours?
He did not have it in hand.
phrases.notes: Literally "it was not in his hand." He had no answer ready.

phrases.english: Jars of gentiles,
phrases.notes: These are jars that were used to store gentiles' wine.

phrases.english: are they forbidden or permitted?
He did not have it in hand.
In what did Moshe serve
all seven days of the inauguration?
He did not have it in hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר עוּקְבָא אִיקְּלַע לְגִינְזַק בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that brings back the question of part-day fasts and adds two unrelated questions
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do part-day fasts count? Are gentile wine jars permitted? What did משה wear during the מילואים?

steps.title: The בית מדרש answers all three questions
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש rules that a part-day fast counts and gets תפלת תענית, that gentile jars are permitted after twelve months, and that משה served in a white robe.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and asked in the בית מדרש. They told him: The הלכה is that one can fast for part of a day and say the fast-day prayer. The הלכה is that gentiles' jars are permitted after twelve months. What did משה wear when he served all seven days of the מילואים? A white robe.
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא brings the three questions to the בית מדרש, and they answer each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer settles our topic: a part-day fast is a real fast and gets תפלת תענית, which matches אביי's reading of רב הונא. The jars are not forbidden forever; after twelve months without use they are permitted. משה did not serve in the כהנים' special garments. He wore a white robe.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה: a part-day fast counts and gets תפלת תענית; gentile wine jars are permitted after twelve months; משה served in a white robe.

phrases.english: He went and asked in the study hall.
They said to him: The halacha is:
one does fast for hours,
and one prays the fast-day prayer,
and the halacha is: jars of gentiles,
after twelve months, are permitted.
phrases.notes: He means twelve months in which the jars were not used.

phrases.english: In what did Moshe serve
all seven days of the inauguration?
In a white robe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל וּשְׁאֵיל בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answers to the three questions from step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A part-day fast counts and gets תפלת תענית; the jars are permitted after twelve months; משה wore a white robe.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the robe had no hem
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא's version adds that משה's white robe had no hem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא taught: In a white robe that has no hem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא teaches the answer about משה's clothing in his own version, adding one detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that משה wore a white robe. He adds that the robe had no hem, which describes it more exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: A hem or border on a garment

phrases.english: Rav Kahana taught:
In a white robe that has no hem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more detailed version of the answer about משה's garment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה served in a white robe that had no hem.

steps.title: רב חסדא is introduced as the next speaker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new teaching from רב חסדא. Only the opening words appear here. His actual statement follows right after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by naming a new speaker, רב חסדא. His actual teaching has not appeared yet; it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'אמר' line names who is about to speak, so the learner knows a new statement is coming. Nothing has been ruled or argued yet. Treat this line as the doorway to the next teaching, not as a teaching of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement or teaching said by a named חכם.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a ruling in this line. It only tells you who is about to speak. The content comes in the next line of the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: None. This is just the attribution that opens a מימרא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the rulings about part-day fasts, gentile jars and משה's white robe (steps 11-13). It begins a new teaching by a different חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. This line only introduces רב חסדא as the speaker. His ruling follows in the next part of the text.
